title: Vietnamese Medical Interpretation Best Practices
summary: Practical guidance for Vietnamese medical interpretation, medication communication, written translation, and quality review in healthcare.
body_markdown:
###


Confirm the patient’s preferred spoken and written language, whether the patient and interpreter understand each other comfortably, who is participating, how the patient wants family involved, and whether hearing, speech, vision, or literacy needs affect the plan.


###


Not automatically. Regional varieties can differ in pronunciation and vocabulary, but individual comprehension matters most. Ask whether the patient and interpreter understand each other, clarify unfamiliar terms, and change interpreters or modes if communication remains difficult.


###


No. Interpretation supports a live conversation, while translation produces written text. They use different inputs, evaluation methods, and quality controls. Evidence about one AI translation system should not be generalized to live interpretation.


###


State the medication, dose, unit, route, frequency, and duration clearly. Avoid unexplained abbreviations, pause for interpretation, and ask the patient to explain when and how they will take the medication.


###


Use the organization’s escalation pathway when the patient requests a human interpreter, meaning remains uncertain after repetition, audio is unreliable, the language variety or task has not been adequately evaluated, or organizational policy calls for human support.
